post4.title: Code Reusability in Daily Programming Work
post4.excerpt: When working on any project, it's natural to find yourself repeating the same code multiple times in different places. Instead of copy-pasting, you should think about code reusability to save time, reduce errors, and make maintenance easier.
post4.fullContent:
When working on any project, it's natural to find yourself repeating the same code multiple times in different places. Instead of copy-pasting, you should think about code reusability to save time, reduce errors, and make maintenance easier.

Why Should You Think About Reusability?

1. You'll Save Time and Effort

Instead of writing the same thing every time, you can use it directly wherever you need it.

2. You'll Reduce Bugs

When you reuse code instead of rewriting it every time, the chance of making mistakes decreases because this code has been tested before.

3. Maintenance Will Be Easier

If you need to modify something, you'll change it in one place only, not in 10 different files.

4. You'll Work Faster

When you have ready-to-use reusable components, you won't have to write everything from scratch every time, and you'll accomplish tasks faster.

How to Make Your Code Reusable?

1. Break Down Code into Small Components (Componentization)

In React, for example, instead of writing the same code everywhere, create a Component that you can use anywhere.

Example: Reusable Button in React

const Button = ({ label, onClick, variant = "primary" }) => { return ( <button className={`btn btn-${variant}`} onClick={onClick}> {label} </button> ); };

Here, instead of writing the button code every time, anyone on the team can use it easily.

2. Use Hooks Instead of Repetition

If you have logic that repeats in more than one Component, it's better to make it a Hook instead of writing it every time.

Example: Hook for Managing Loading State

const useLoading = () => { const [loading, setLoading] = useState(false); const startLoading = () => setLoading(true); const stopLoading = () => setLoading(false); return { loading, startLoading, stopLoading }; };

This way, instead of creating useState for loading in every Component, you can use this Hook directly.

3. Leverage Utility Functions

If you have logic that repeats in more than one place, make it a single Function and put it in a separate file.

Example: Function to Convert Text to a Suitable Title (Slugify)

export const slugify = (text: string) => { return text.toLowerCase().replace(/\s+/g, "-").replace(/[^\w-]+/g, ""); };

Now anyone who needs to convert text to a slug can use this function instead of writing the code themselves every time.

Conclusion

Code reusability is not a luxury, it's a skill that makes you faster, your work cleaner, and errors fewer. For any code you feel you're repeating, think about how to reuse it? You'll find solutions like:

  • ✅ Breaking down code into small components (Components).
  • ✅ Using Hooks in React instead of repetition.
  • ✅ Storing repeated code in Utility Functions.

Try this approach and you'll feel a big difference in your work style!

post6.title: React 19.2 - The New Update Worth Trying
post6.excerpt: React released a new update on October 1, 2025. Version 19.2 was released with some additions and improvements that are really worth trying, especially if you're working on large projects or apps with a lot of interaction between the frontend and server.
post6.fullContent:
React released a new update on October 1, 2025. Version 19.2 was released with some additions and improvements that are really worth trying, especially if you're working on large projects or apps with a lot of interaction between the frontend and server.

Let me explain briefly — what's new? And what's been changed?

1. Activity Component

This is a completely new component from React. The idea is that you can divide the UI into separate activities and control when they appear and when they hide.

For example, if you have many pages open at the same time, you can make React hide activities that are not visible and save performance, and as soon as you return to them again, React restores them quickly without reloading them from scratch.

There are two basic states:

  • visible: The activity is visible and working normally.
  • hidden: The activity is hidden, React temporarily stops the effects and saves resources.

2. useEffectEvent Hook

This hook is honestly brilliant. How many times have you encountered useEffect running repeatedly because a simple dependency changed?

This hook solves this problem. It allows you to separate event logic (like event handlers) from the effect itself, so React won't re-execute the effect repeatedly unnecessarily.

3. cacheSignal

This is specifically made for React Server Components. It gives you a signal to know when the cache has expired or the render is complete or cancelled.

This is very useful in applications with data caching or SSR.

4. Performance Tracks in DevTools

The biggest addition for developers! Now React DevTools has new performance tracks that show exactly what's happening inside React:

  • When rendering starts
  • When scheduling happens
  • How it handles priorities

This means we can finally understand why a certain component is slowing down or delayed.

5. Partial Pre-rendering

This feature allows you to pre-render part of the page and send it to the client quickly, then continue loading the rest of the data later.

This means users will see the page much faster, especially in projects with dynamic content.

Important Improvements and Fixes

React 19.2 also includes some important fixes and improvements:

  • Improved SSR rendering with Suspense boundaries so content is collected and displayed in a coordinated manner.
  • Web Streams support in Node.js for higher performance with renderToReadableStream.
  • Changed the useId prefix from :r: to _r_ for XML compatibility.
  • Updated eslint-plugin-react-hooks to version 6.1.1 which supports new hooks like useEffectEvent.
  • Also fixes in useDeferredValue, form submission, and Hot Reload.

My Personal Opinion

Honestly, React 19 was a huge leap, but 19.2 took the important second step: improving developer experience, not just application performance.

If you're working on enterprise projects or dealing with server components, this version will make a big difference for you, especially with the new performance tools and the pre-rendering feature that actually significantly improves user experience.

post7.title: Quick Info: What's the Difference Between GitHub and GitLab?
post7.excerpt: Many of us use GitHub and GitLab on a daily basis, but what's the difference between them?
post7.fullContent:
Many of us use GitHub and GitLab on a daily basis, but what's the difference between them?

1. GitHub

  • A hosted platform for code management using Git.
  • Very popular, and used more in open source projects.
  • Supports collaboration between developers through Pull Requests and code reviews.
  • Has GitHub Actions that help with automation (CI/CD).
  • Owned by Microsoft.

2. GitLab

  • A platform similar to GitHub but focuses more on continuous integration and continuous delivery (CI/CD) as a core part.
  • Can be self-hosted on your own server, which gives it an advantage in companies that need full control.
  • Has advanced project management features like bug tracking and release planning.
  • More suitable for companies that want a comprehensive solution for DevOps management.

Summary

If you're working on open source projects or want an easy-to-use platform, GitHub might be the best choice.

If you need integrated DevOps tools or have a company and want to host the platform internally, GitLab is the strongest solution.

I hope you benefited from this post 😃🤍

post8.title: Managing Large Frontend Projects Using Module Federation
post8.excerpt: In large frontend projects, things start to get complicated when the number of teams increases and each team works on a separate part. This is where Module Federation appears as a practical and smart solution to this problem.
post8.fullContent:
Today I'm here to talk to you about managing large frontend projects using Module Federation.

In large frontend projects, things start to get complicated when the number of teams increases and each team works on a separate part. This is where Module Federation appears as a practical and smart solution to this problem.

What is Module Federation?

In short, this is a feature in Webpack 5 that allows you to share components or libraries between different applications without merging them during the Build. This means instead of each application being isolated, applications communicate with each other at runtime.

Why might you need it?

  1. Work Division: Each team works on a part of the project independently.
  2. Time Saving: Instead of building the entire application every time, you update a small part.
  3. Code Reuse: Any component you share works in more than one application without publishing it to npm.

Simple Practical Example

If you have two applications:

  • App1: The main application.
  • App2: Contains shared components like a button.

1. In App2:

module.exports = { plugins: [ new ModuleFederationPlugin({ name: "App2", filename: "remoteEntry.js", exposes: { "./Button": "./src/components/Button", }, }), ], };

2. In App1:

module.exports = { plugins: [ new ModuleFederationPlugin({ remotes: { App2: "App2@http://localhost:3002/remoteEntry.js", }, }), ], };

3. Use the component like this:

const Button = React.lazy(() => import("App2/Button"));

When to use it?

  • If your team is large and everyone is working on a different part.
  • If you want to reduce build time and improve performance.
  • If you have old projects and want to add new features to them.

Summary

Module Federation is a tool that will help you build your large projects in a more organized and flexible way. Try it and share your experience or questions in the comments!

I hope you benefited 😃🤍

post9.title: How to Use What We Learn in Academic Curricula in Practical Life?
post9.excerpt: Throughout the study period, we learn many things like data structures and algorithms, but rarely does anyone tell us what to use them for or how.
post9.fullContent:
Throughout the study period, we learn many things like data structures and algorithms, but rarely does anyone tell us what to use them for or how. This gap between theory and practice makes people feel that education is not connected to reality. So, how do we bridge this gap?

Data structures and algorithms are the foundation of everything we do in computer science. Whether you're working in software development, data analysis, or artificial intelligence, you'll find yourself dealing with these concepts every day. For example, understanding how Linked Lists work can help improve the performance of applications that need to insert and delete elements quickly. And algorithms like Sorting Algorithms can be crucial in organizing data efficiently.

To understand more how to use these concepts, we need to see real examples like:

Performance Improvement

When we face a performance problem in a program, we can use search and sorting algorithms to improve response speed.

Data Management

Using different data structures like Trees and Hash Tables can help organize data and access it quickly.

Problem Solving

Algorithms help us find optimal solutions to complex problems like the shortest path in networks (Shortest Path in Graphs).

Professors and curriculum supervisors have a very important role in bridging the gap between theory and practice. Some strategies they can follow, for example:

Providing Real Examples

Presenting examples from real life where data structures and algorithms are used.

Practical Projects

Assigning students to practical projects that force them to use theoretical concepts in solving real problems.

Industry Interaction

Inviting professionals from the industry to talk about how they use these concepts in their daily work.

In Conclusion

It's very important to move beyond the stage of just throwing information at students and help them understand how to use this knowledge in their practical lives. By presenting real examples and practical applications, we can make education more connected and valuable. These steps will help better prepare students to face real-world challenges with confidence and knowledge.

post10.excerpt: In the age of technology, you need to have an idea about the best user interface (UI) development libraries because they make a huge difference in user experience.
post10.fullContent:
Hello, I'd like to talk to you today about user interface development libraries.

In the age of technology, you need to have an idea about the best user interface (UI) development libraries because they make a huge difference in user experience. Today we'll talk about four very important libraries: Tailwind CSS, Bootstrap, Material-UI (MUI), and Bulma.

1. Tailwind CSS

The first thing you need to know about Tailwind is that it makes styling easier when designing. It gives you great opportunities for customization and precise element modification, and provides fast and comfortable performance.

2. Bootstrap

Bootstrap is the one that understands you, if you want to start quickly and finish your work easily, here's the solution. Bootstrap provides ready-made components and flexibility in use, and helps you design an excellent user interface.

3. Material-UI (MUI)

If you're a React enthusiast, you'll love Material-UI. It provides a large collection of components and tools with modern and distinctive design, and gives you a great user experience.

4. Bulma

Bulma is simple and easy, considered an excellent choice for small and medium projects. It provides easily modifiable and customizable CSS classes, and gives you great designs easily.

Summary

Whatever your project, you need to choose the appropriate library that meets your needs. Choose the one that makes development easier for you and gives you a distinctive user experience, and enjoy building great and impressive designs.

post11.title: Improve code quality with ESLint
post11.excerpt: In the fast-paced world of software development, maintaining code quality is crucial. ESLint is a powerful and versatile tool that can help you write clean, maintainable, and error-free JavaScript code.
post11.fullContent:
In the fast-paced world of software development, maintaining code quality is crucial. The larger your code base, the harder it is to ensure consistency, catch bugs, and follow best practices. This is where ESLint comes into play. ESLint is a powerful and versatile tool that can help you write clean, maintainable, and error-free JavaScript code. In this article, we'll explore what ESLint is, why it's important, and how you can leverage it to improve your development workflow.

What is ESLint?

ESLint is an open source static code analysis tool that helps developers identify and fix problems in their JavaScript code. It is highly configurable, allowing you to define and implement coding standards and best practices within your project. ESLint scans your code for potential issues, style violations, and security concerns, helping you catch bugs early in the development process.

Why ESLint matters:

1. Code consistency

ESLint enforces coding standards and style guidelines, ensuring that all team members follow a consistent coding style. This consistency makes the code base easy to read and maintain.

2. Error Detection

ESLint can detect common programming errors, such as undefined variables, misspelled function names, or incorrect use of JavaScript features. It helps you identify and fix these problems before they cause runtime errors.

3. Security

ESLint can help identify vulnerabilities, such as potentially unsafe patterns or code that may lead to vulnerabilities such as cross-site scripting (XSS) or SQL injection.

4. Code Quality

By highlighting code smells and encouraging best practices, ESLint contributes to raising code quality, making your application more robust and easier to maintain.

Getting started with ESLint:

To start using ESLint, follow these steps:

1. Installation

You can install ESLint globally or locally in your project using npm or yarn. It is usually best to install it locally to manage project-specific configurations.

2. Configuration

ESLint relies on a configuration file (usually called ".eslintrc.js" or ".eslintrc.json") to define the coding standards for your project. You can use common presets or create a custom configuration that suits your project's needs.

3. Integration with your IDE

ESLint can be integrated with most popular code editors and integrated development environments (IDEs). These integrations will highlight issues in real-time as you code.

4. Run ESLint

You can run ESLint from the command line or configure it as part of the build process. It will analyze your code and report any issues it finds.

Customize ESLint rules:

One of ESLint's strengths is its flexibility. You can customize its rules to suit the specific requirements of your project. ESLint provides an extensive list of rules that you can enable, disable, or configure. For example, you can force code indentation, require the use of single or double quotes, and ensure proper variable naming conventions.

post12.title: Harnessing the Benefits of Lazy Loading in React Apps
post12.excerpt: Lazy Loading is a performance optimization technique used in web applications. It essentially means loading content or elements only when they become visible to the user.
post12.fullContent:
Hello, my LinkedIn connections!

Today, I'd like to share some thoughts on the topic of Lazy Loading and how it can make a significant difference in React applications. This technology is undeniably one of the cornerstones of a great user experience and can bring about numerous advantages when implemented correctly.

What is Lazy Loading?

Lazy Loading is a performance optimization technique used in web applications. It essentially means loading content or elements only when they become visible to the user. This reduces initial loading times and enhances application responsiveness.

Utilizing Lazy Loading in React:

In React applications, we can use "React Lazy" and "React Suspense" to effectively implement deferred loading. Instead of loading all components upfront, we load them only when they are needed by the user. This provides a substantial boost in application performance and ensures a swift response to user interactions.

Benefits of Lazy Loading in React:

Improved Application Performance

We can reduce initial loading times and enhance navigation speed within the application.

Memory Efficiency

Components are loaded only when they are required, thus conserving memory resources.

Enhanced User Experience

Users can quickly access the content they want to see without significant waiting times.

Conclusion

Implementing Lazy Loading in React is a fantastic choice for improving application performance and delivering a superior user experience. Let's work together to enhance our applications, making them more sustainable and faster.

Feel free to share your thoughts and experiences! #React #LazyLoading #PerformanceOptimization
